fonte: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Mendell, Nov. 8, 1886, in the Annual Report of the Chief of Engineers, 1888)
legenda: Draft: how deep a ship sits in the water. Ceiling: 18 or 20 ft at high water.
texto_para_tela: NOV. 8, 1886 · 12–14 FT · 18 OR 20 FT AT HIGH WATER
credito_tela: Source: Annual Report of the Chief of Engineers, U.S. Army, 1888
nota: O 12–14 é descrição do engenheiro, não sondagem publicada; o 18 ou 20 é previsão de teto, não medição, e está em maré alta.
narracao: In between came the letter. On November 8, 1886, Colonel Mendell signed it in San Francisco. Wilmington harbor, he wrote, already took ships drawing twelve to fourteen feet, meaning they sat that deep in the water. And still he wrote: "It is a small estuary and can never be made a harbor for deep-water ships." His next sentence set the ceiling: if eighteen or twenty feet at high water could be obtained, the harbor would have reached its maximum development.
